test.title: Mini-test · The sounds of a coral reef

paragraphs.text: Healthy coral reefs are noisy places. Fish grunt and click, and snapping shrimp produce a constant crackling sound. Marine scientists have discovered that these noises are important for the young fish that will one day live on the reef.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: After hatching, the larvae of many reef fish drift in the open ocean for several weeks. When they are ready to settle, they swim towards reefs, and experiments show that they are guided partly by sound, which travels well under water.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Damaged reefs are much quieter. In 2017, a team working off the coast of northern Australia recorded reefs that had lost most of their coral after a heatwave and found that they produced less than half the sound of healthy reefs.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The researchers then tried an unusual experiment. They placed underwater loudspeakers on patches of dead coral and played recordings of healthy reefs for six weeks. These patches attracted twice as many young fish as silent patches nearby.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: The team stresses that sound alone cannot restore a reef. Young fish will not stay unless there is food and shelter, and the coral itself will only recover if water temperatures remain stable. However, loudspeakers could help to speed up recovery in areas where new coral has already been planted.
paragraphs.label: E
